title: Faster Blue Tongue & EHD Vaccination: Minister Clarinval's Outlook
text:
Farmers adn livestock owners are seeing positive strides in the ongoing effort to protect their animals, with the latest figures showing a significant increase in vaccinations. This article provides an in-depth look at the current status of the livestock vaccination campaign against Bluetongue and EHD , and the anticipated timeline for complete coverage. Learn how the campaign is progressing and what it means for the health of your livestock.
Livestock Vaccination Campaign Gains Momentum; Officials Anticipate Full Coverage by Late May Published: 2025-04-09
Vaccination Progress and Future Deliveries As of early April, vaccination efforts against the BTV3 variant of the Blauwtong virus and Epizootic Hemorrhagic Disease (EHD) are underway, with important progress reported in sheep and cattle populations. Minister Clarinval assured the public that vaccine availability is not a concern, and ample deliveries are expected to facilitate complete livestock vaccination by the end of May.
Vaccination Rates: A Snapshot According to the “campaign Barometer” from FPS public Health, vaccination rates vary across different animal populations and vaccine types:
Sheep (BTV3): Over 39% vaccinated. Cattle (BTV3): Nearly 38% vaccinated. Cattle (EHD): Approximately 21% vaccinated. The minister noted that thes figures are steadily increasing each week.
Comparative Analysis: March 20 vs.Current While progress is evident, a comparison with figures from March 20 reveals subtle shifts in vaccination rates:
cattle (BTV3 – March 20): Almost 30% vaccinated. Cattle (EHDV – March 20): 18% vaccinated. Cattle ( BTV8 – March 20): Only 1.5% vaccinated. Sheep (BTV3 – March 20): 39% vaccinated. Notably,vaccination rates for the blauwtong vaccine BTV8 remain low,with only 2.14% of cattle and 2.81% of sheep having received the BTV4 vaccine.
minister Clarinval’s Optimistic Outlook Minister Clarinval commended the collaborative efforts of farmers and veterinarians in the ongoing vaccination campaign.He emphasized the impact of these joint efforts:
The new deliveries that we receive in the coming weeks will enable us to vaccinate the entire livestock by the end of May.
Minister Clarinval
Understanding the Viruses Blauwtong (Bluetongue): Blauwtong is a non-contagious, insect-borne, viral disease of ruminants, mainly sheep, but also cattle, goats, deer, and camelids. The disease is caused by the Bluetongue virus (BTV). Different serotypes of the virus exist, hence the references to BTV3, BTV4 and BTV8. Vaccination is a key preventative measure.
Epizootic Hemorrhagic Disease (EHD): EHD is another insect-borne,viral disease that primarily affects deer,but can also infect cattle. Like Bluetongue, it is indeed not directly contagious between animals.
Looking Ahead With consistent vaccine deliveries and continued collaboration between farmers and veterinarians, authorities are optimistic about achieving complete livestock vaccination by the projected deadline. The focus remains on maintaining momentum and addressing the lower vaccination rates for specific vaccine types to ensure broad protection against prevalent diseases.
